summary.intent: Execute Phase 23 (rust-sdk-extraction) using wave-based parallel subagent execution, extracting crypto, core types, API client, FUSE filesystem, and SDK orchestration into a Cargo workspace.
summary.outcome: Waves 1 and 2 completed successfully (plans 23-01 through 23-03). Wave 3 (plans 23-04 and 23-05) was interrupted mid-execution by a usage limit reset; partial crate directory structures were created but not committed. Wave 3 was re-spawned on resume, with fuse crate files partially written.

repo: Phase 23 uses branch `feat/phase-23-rust-sdk-extraction` with a 4-wave dependency chain: crypto → core+api-client → fuse+sdk → desktop-cleanup+CI
The Cargo workspace root and `crates/` directory structure was established in wave 1 as the foundation all subsequent crates depend on
162 existing desktop tests remained passing after wave 2 extractions, and 12 new core crate tests were added
Wave 3 agents (23-04, 23-05) began creating crate directories but produced no lib.rs or committed code before the usage limit hit

workflow: Usage limit interruptions leave uncommitted partial work in the working tree — spot-checking git log and file presence is necessary to distinguish 'no work done' from 'work done but not committed'
GSD resumption works by re-spawning agents for plans lacking SUMMARY.md; agents must handle pre-existing partial crate directories gracefully
Pre-wave dependency checks (verify key-links) returned nothing to verify for wave 3 plans, suggesting key-link metadata was absent from those plan files

friction: Usage limit reset mid-execution during Wave 3 parallel agent spawning, leaving both 23-04 and 23-05 with uncommitted partial state
After resume, no SUMMARY.md existed for either Wave 3 plan, requiring manual diagnosis of partial crate state before re-spawning
The fuse crate was missing lib.rs and most modules; the sdk crate was missing lib.rs and client.rs — indicating agents were mid-task when interrupted
